extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians organizing or presenting at AMS (and joint MAA) meetings; Associate Secretaries and session organizers
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural guidance for proposing, organizing, announcing, and submitting abstracts for AMS Special Sessions, Invited Addresses, and contributed paper sessions (including MAA joint-session procedures) at Sectional, Annual, and Joint Meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Invited Addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Invited addresses at Sectional Meetings are selected by the Section Program Committee, usually twelve to eighteen months in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members wishing to nominate candidates should send relevant information to the Associate Secretary for the Section who will forward it to the Section Program Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Sessions selection by PCNM
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Sessions at Annual and Summer Meetings are selected by the Program Committee for National Meetings (PCNM) from a list of proposed Special Sessions in essentially the same manner as individuals are selected to give Invited Addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The number of Special Sessions at a Summer or Annual Meeting is limited; the algorithm determining the number is given in the "Rules for Special Sessions" (referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for Special Session proposals (nine-month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that are to be considered must be in the hands of the PCNM at least nine months prior to the meeting at which the Special Session is to be held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lead time ensures the committee may consider all proposals simultaneously; proposals sent to Providence, to the Notices, or to anyone other than the Associate Secretary may have to be forwarded and may not be received in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Session announcement timing for abstracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Sessions must be announced in the Notices in such a timely fashion that any member who wishes may submit an abstract for consideration for presentation in the Special Session before the deadline for such consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This deadline is usually three weeks before the deadline for abstracts for the meeting in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of first refusal for Special Session proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Society reserves the right of first refusal for the publication of proceedings of any Special Session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These proceedings appear in the book series Contemporary Mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission route for Special Session proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals to organize a Special Session may be submitted to the Associate Secretary in charge of that meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals sent elsewhere (to the Providence office, to the Notices, or to anyone other than the Associate Secretary) will have to be forwarded and may not be received in time to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectional Meetings processing parity
rubrics_metrics.description: Processing of proposals for Special Sessions for Sectional Meetings is handled in essentially the same manner as for Annual and Summer Meetings by the Section Program Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No Special Session at a Sectional Meeting may be approved so late that its announcement appears past the deadline after which members can no longer send abstracts for consideration for presentation in that Special Session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract receipt requirement for program listing (Council decree)
rubrics_metrics.description: No paper, whether invited or contributed, may be listed in the program of a meeting of the Society unless an abstract of the paper has been received in Providence prior to the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstracts of papers submitted for consideration for presentation at a Special Session must be received by the Providence office by the special deadline for Special Sessions (usually three weeks earlier than the deadline for contributed papers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission of AMS abstracts (TeX users)
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic submission of abstracts is available to those who use the TeX typesetting system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests to obtain the package of files may be sent electronically via the Internet to abs-request@math.ams.com. When requesting the abstracts package, users should specify whether they want the plain TeX, AMS-TeX, or the LaTeX package. Only abstracts should be sent to abs-submit@math.ams.com. Questions regarding an abstract should be addressed to abs-misc@math.ams.com; meeting questions to meet@math.ams.com.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and joint authorship rules for presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual may present only one ten-minute contributed paper at a meeting; joint authorship combinations may be accepted provided no individual speaks more than once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An author can speak by invitation in more than one Special Session at the same meeting. An individual may contribute only one abstract by title in any one issue of Abstracts, but joint authors are treated as a separate category (so, in addition to abstracts from two individual authors, one joint abstract by them may be accepted).

rubrics_metrics.name: AMS contributed paper abstract procedures and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts for AMS contributed paper sessions should be prepared on the standard AMS form and sent to Abstracts, Meetings Department, American Mathematical Society, P.O. Box 6887, Providence, RI 02940, to arrive by the abstract deadline of October 8, 1992.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A charge of $16 is imposed for retyping abstracts that are not in camera-ready form. Late papers will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint Meetings: indicating suitability for AMS Special Sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: For Joint Meetings, anyone contributing an abstract who feels their paper would be particularly appropriate for an AMS Special Session should indicate this clearly on the abstract and should submit it by September 18, 1992 (three weeks earlier than the normal deadline) to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preliminary indication helps consider the paper for inclusion in Special Sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAA contributed sessions: one-page summary requirement (new procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: For MAA contributed paper sessions, the name(s) and address(es) of the author(s) and a one-page summary of the paper should be sent directly to the organizer; the summary must reach the organizer by September 10, 1992.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary is to enable the organizer(s) to evaluate appropriateness for the session and should be as detailed and informative as possible within the one-page limit. Summaries should NOT be sent to the MAA Washington office. The organizer will acknowledge receipt and, if accepted, will send a standardized abstract form to be used to prepare a brief abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAA contributed sessions: abstract form and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper is accepted for presentation in an MAA session, the organizer will send the author(s) a standardized abstract form; completed abstract forms must be returned to the organizer promptly and no later than September 24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send the abstracts to the AMS, and do not submit them electronically. Abstracts not received by that date cannot be published. An abstract form may be obtained in advance from the AMS or MAA offices and submitted with the summary if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation length limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentations are normally limited to ten minutes, although selected contributors may be given up to twenty minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to contributed presentations; invited papers and session scheduling may differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: MAA session room equipment and requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Rooms where MAA contributed paper sessions will be held are equipped with an overhead projector and screen; blackboards are not available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persons having other equipment needs should contact the MAA Associate Secretary as soon as possible, but in any case prior to November 9. Upon request, one additional overhead, a 35mm carousel slide projector, or a 1/2" or 3/4" VHS video cassette recorder with one color monitor will be made available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site selection timing and host department responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Sectional Meeting sites are recommended by the Associate Secretary for the Section and approved by the Committee of Associate Secretaries and Secretary, usually eighteen to twenty-four months in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host departments supply local information, ten to twelve rooms with overhead projectors for contributed paper sessions and Special Sessions, an auditorium with twin overhead projectors for invited addresses, and registration clerks. The Society partially reimburses for rental of facilities, equipment, and staffing the registration desk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and deadlines guidance for Meetings and Conferences listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcements will be published in the Notices if they contain a call for papers and specify place, date, subject, speakers, deadlines for abstracts/contributed papers, and source of further information; a second announcement is published only for changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listings should be received in Providence SIX MONTHS prior to the scheduled date to appear in more than one issue; entries for Meetings and Conferences have deadlines listed on the inside front cover of each issue. Effective with the 1990 volume, the complete list is published only in the September issue; other issues carry meetings for the following twelve-month period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forwarding risk for misaddressed proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals that are sent to the Providence office, to the Notices, or directed to anyone other than the Associate Secretary will have to be forwarded and may not be received in time to be considered for acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit proposals directly to the Associate Secretary in charge of the meeting to avoid forwarding delays.
